title: Atalanta 4-4 Inter: Last-gasp Kessie penalty settles Serie A thriller
subtitle: Inter kept extending their lead against Atalanta, but in the end, they could not hold out for all three points.
paragraphs: Franck Kessie's stoppage-time penalty earned Atalanta a deserved point in a thrilling 4-4 draw with Inter in Serie A.
Inter had been cruising thanks to Francesco Pio Esposito's hat-trick, despite Eljif Elmas pulling one back before the break for the hosts at New Balance Arena.
But Charles De Ketelaere scored a brace on either side of Petar Sucic's penalty, and Kessie salvaged the draw to settle the breathless encounter.
Nicolo Barella's first cross was blocked straight back to him, and his follow-up was deflected to Esposito, who swept Inter into a 16th-minute lead.

Marco Sportiello then made a brilliant double save to keep out Marcus Thuram and Esposito. But from the resulting corner, Federico Dimarco whipped in a brilliant delivery to pick out the unmarked Esposito, who thumped in a header in the 32nd minute.
Atalanta had a lifeline three minutes later, though, with Elmas recovering after missing the ball with his first attempt to fire past Josep Martinez.
Esposito completed his hat-trick seven minutes after the break; Thuram cut Atalanta's defence wide open with his throughball and the Italian striker duly finished off the move.
Atalanta refused to lie down, though, and De Ketelaere rose highest at a corner to head past Martinez with 72 minutes on the clock, bringing the hosts back within one goal.

Straight from the restart, Inter attacked through Thuram, whose low cross was cleared off the line by Davide Zappacosta, who tripped as he did so, ultimately diverting the ball off the line with his hand.

Sucic restored Inter's two-goal cushion with a confident 76th-minute penalty, but Atalanta pulled another one back, with De Ketelaere rifling an emphatic finish into the roof of the net in the 80th minute.
Moments before, Martinez had kept out the Belgian from close range, and the Inter goalkeeper was also alert to get a strong hand behind Mario Pasalic's long-range drive.
But he was finally beaten for the fourth time in the 91st minute after Alessandro Bastoni was penalised for a handball in the box, and Kessie slotted in the equaliser from the spot.
Esposito stars but misses out on the headlines
It looked like the day was going to belong to Esposito, who scored his first hat-trick for Inter in a commanding first 52 minutes for the visitors.

In fact, at 21 years and 147 days, he is the fourth-youngest player to score more than 11 goals (12) for Inter in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era (since 1994-95), after Mario Balotelli, Obafemi Martins and Ronaldo.
However, Atalanta never let Inter out of their sights for long and continuously plugged away at their comeback to ensure they did not walk away empty-handed.
Inter edged the shot count (16 to 15) and expected goals tally (3.38 xG to 3.1), but Atalanta got 10 of their attempts on target to just six for Cristian Chivu's side.
While Esposito led the way, having five of those shots and accruing 1.93 xG himself, Atalanta split the load, with each of Kessie, De Ketelaere, Elmas and Krstovic having three shots apiece.

Atalanta have not won any of their last 16 Serie A matches against Inter (D7 L9), but this result will feel like a victory, while Inter will be disappointed, having missed the chance to move within one point of leaders Lazio.
